CORRECTION to the drafted goal, recorded during implementation as required by the append-only ledger. The goal asserted that verification/checks.ts:44 returns a vacuous ReplayIntegrity pass on this repository and that every green validate/govern/full-govern run carried it. That is FALSE and was measured wrong. buildVerificationContext (src/verification/context.ts:53-63) already builds the partition-aware store: createInfra returns a PartitionedEventStore, eventStore.loadAll() returns 448 events here, hasEventLog is true, and `synth verify` reports ReplayIntegrity pass with the message 'Chain valid, replay consistent, graph valid (448 events)'. All six checks pass on real evidence. What IS true, and is the defect this expedition fixes: (1) verifyReplayHealth (src/cli/synth.ts:862-869) tests only sdk.paths.eventLogFile(root) - the legacy single file - so `synth checkpoint` reports 'No event log present; replay skipped' for a ledger holding 448 events; (2) the same legacy-path-only assumption is served to operators and agents by explain paths, explain observability, explain replay-light, first-contact (746, 780, 826) and bootstrap-apply:235, none of which mention the event-stream layout that actually exists on disk; (3) a genuinely empty project still reports ReplayIntegrity as pass rather than as a non-result, because CheckStatus (verification/types.ts:14) has no skipped value; (4) three log layouts coexist with no single resolver. Scope narrows accordingly: the verification engine is NOT broken and must not be rewritten; the presence-and-location question is answered in seven places by one wrong path, and that is what gets unified.

PREMISE CONTRADICTION recorded by measurement before this expedition is started (operator decision 2026-10-13). This expedition is scoped to 'Use ParallelRunner for deterministic checks with no dependencies after build ... measure speedup for govern --full', which frames parallelism as an OPTIMIZATION INSIDE the incremental-selection model: select a subset by blast radius, then parallelize the deterministic ones. Measurement says selection is the broken part and parallelism should be the primary strategy over the whole suite. EVIDENCE 1 - the selector narrows when it should widen. For a change to src/verification/{checks,context,engine,types}.ts, src/cli/synth.ts and src/infra/event-store.ts, `govern-profiler.js --dry-run --explain --profile pull-request` returned risk high, affectedClasses [kernel], checkCount 8, run 5, skip 3: it ran `test` (which is 4 files: synth, proposal-evaluation, governance-evaluation-enforcement, convergence-certification), test:adversarial, test:freeze-certification, typecheck and build, and SKIPPED test:all, govern and proof. The suite that guards the edited dry-run code (tests/lifecycle-dry-run.test.js) is neither in the chain nor selected. High risk produced a narrower run. EVIDENCE 2 - the map behind it is nearly empty: scripts/governance/check-registry.js holds 7 checks with 22 input globs, only 3 of which name a test file; 10 of 169 tasks declare `capabilities`; test:all declares none and estimates 600000 ms against 334 s measured. The engine around it is 3191 lines across 17 modules. EVIDENCE 3 - exhaustive is already cheaper than selective. `npm run test:all` (127 of 242 files, 117 `npm run` invocations) took 5m34s and exited 0. All 242 files run serially took 8m20s. All 242 at 8-way parallel on a 2-core box took 4m11s - i.e. running EVERYTHING in parallel is faster than the current chain running 52% of the files. 183 of 242 files finish in under 2s; the top 3 are 20% of total time and the top 10 are 43%, so duration-balanced sharding, not selection, is what buys the wall clock. RE-SCOPE: ParallelRunner should shard the whole suite by measured duration; selection should be reserved for the expensive or environment-dependent tail (3 files over 30s, benchmarks, certification, and the suites needing sibling workspace packages built). EXP-TEST-005 (74c33996d5e7cf32) owns the file inventory and ownership guard that any sharder needs; do not build a file-level inventory here. MEASUREMENT METHOD, corrected after getting it wrong once: 'measure speedup' must record nproc and the parallelism factor, and must say whether per-file durations were taken solo or contended. A first pass at P=8 on 2 cores inflated per-file durations roughly 4x and produced a false '18.7 min serial for the chain' against a true solo figure of 4.7 min. NEW DEPENDENCY: EXP-CLI-001 (2c13ca22fb8c4e6c) changes the per-process term by about 3x (175.7 ms to load the CLI monolith today, target <=45 ms) and the suite contains 758 CLI-spawn call-sites across 106 files, so per-process cost dominates process count. Any speedup measurement taken before EXP-CLI-001 lands will be obsolete; re-take it after.

MEASURED CENSUS, replacing the static estimate in the goal. The goal said 758 CLI-spawn call-sites and called it a lower bound; the real number is more than double. Instrumented dist/cli/synth.js and dist/cli/entry.js IN PLACE (after the shebang, filenames unchanged - renaming breaks the `path.resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` entry guard, and prepending before the shebang is a SyntaxError; both mistakes were made and corrected) and ran all 242 suites in a throwaway copy at /tmp/sweep3, 2-way parallel on 2 cores, 252s wall. Verified behaviour-preserving first: expedition-lifecycle rc=0 at 31.9s against a 37.7s clean baseline. RESULT: 1572 CLI PROCESS INVOCATIONS per full suite run = 2.07x the 758 static call-sites. ENTRY POINT: 1536 of 1572 (98%) spawn dist/cli/synth.js - the monolith. Only 35 (2%) spawn dist/cli/entry.js, the light dispatcher. The light path is effectively unused by the suite. VERBS: mission 427, expedition 394 (together 52% - governance ceremony), bootstrap 118, first-contact 113, explain 112, init 71, status 60, alignment 38, task 34, then validate/project/doctor/capabilities/log at 14-17 each. TIME: in-process execution AFTER the module graph has loaded is median 55.8 ms, p90 188.2 ms, total 158s. Priced at the independently measured wall cost of a synth.js invocation (152 ms in the copy, 175.7 ms in the real repo), the 1572 calls account for 239-276s = 4.0-4.6 min of the 8m20s full serial suite, of which roughly 2.5-3.1 min is module loading alone. So 30-37% of the entire suite's wall time is spent re-loading the same 2.27 MB, and the commands' own work is the minority of each call. TWO CONSEQUENCES FOR SEQUENCING. (a) The one-line harness change - point tests/helpers/cli-harness.js:24 at entry.js instead of synth.js - moves 1536 calls onto the dispatcher and saves about 75.6 ms each (175.7 -> 100.1 ms measured), i.e. roughly 116s = 1.9 min per full run BEFORE any decomposition happens. It is the cheapest large win available and should not wait for phase 3. (b) Hitting the proposed <=45 ms budget would save 1572 x (152-45) to (176-45) ms = 2.8-3.4 min per full run, about 35-40% of the suite, and cut every interactive call by 3-4x. This also sharpens the EXP-TEST-003 note: with 1572 process spawns, per-process cost dominates process count, so merging suites (EXP-TEST-002) or sharding them (EXP-TEST-003) cannot recover what loading the monolith 1572 times costs.

RESOLUTION AND THREE FURTHER FINDINGS, after the operator restored branch arena/841cc45d-synth on origin (2026-10-13). The delivery record that finding B said could not be produced honestly now exists, and the containment claim finding D called unverifiable is now CORROBORATED by independent git evidence. WHAT WORKED, exactly: (1) `git fetch origin arena/841cc45d-synth:refs/remotes/origin/arena/841cc45d-synth` - a plain `git fetch origin <branch>` was NOT enough, because this clone's refspec is single-branch and the fetch only populated FETCH_HEAD, leaving the name unresolvable. The explicit refspec creates a remote-tracking ref without creating a local branch or moving HEAD. (2) `expedition deliver --id 2c9c6c62a727ece8 --branch origin/arena/841cc45d-synth --no-push` succeeded: EXPEDITION_DELIVERED, commit c7651ce342bb1fc240d00bcd50d23e6d2c3b76c2, tipCommit 64ea89c3626992fc49323aea3b17784686d60023, deliveryPending false. resolveDeliveryBranch's documented origin/ path is the right mechanism and worked as written. (3) Containment was STILL unverifiable at that point: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <tip> <merge>` exited 1 because merge commit 8b8dce26 was grafted with an empty parent list in this shallow clone - the tip object being present is not sufficient. (4) `git fetch --deepen 30 origin` exposed the parents: 8b8dce26 now reports parents [bb8809ae 64ea89c3], and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 64ea89c3... 8b8dce26...` exits 0. CORROBORATED. So deliverable 4 has a concrete recipe to encode: resolve the tip, then test ancestry; if the merge commit is grafted, report 'unavailable (shallow clone; parents not fetched)' with the deepen command as the next step, and only report 'corroborated' when is-ancestor actually exits 0. Never assert containment from the presence of a tip alone. FINDING F - lifecycle order is not enforced in either direction. deliver succeeded on an expedition that was already sealed/integrated. The record now timestamps the inversion: metadata.integration.integratedAt = 457 precedes metadata.delivery.deliveredAt = 462. Nothing refused, warned, or flagged it. Either order must be enforced, or the out-of-order case must be recorded as an anomaly on the face of the record. FINDING G - the delivery record names a REF PATH, not a branch. metadata.delivery.branch was stored as 'origin/arena/841cc45d-synth' (the remote-tracking form used to resolve it) while metadata.executionBranch already holds the canonical 'arena/841cc45d-synth'. resolveDeliveryBranch computes canonicalBranch for exactly this case and the ledger discards it. A delivery record should name the branch; the ref path is how it was found, not what it is. FINDING H - restoring branches is not a scalable fix for the backlog. This one closed because the operator manually recreated the branch on origin. The other 24 derivable delivery-pending expeditions had their head branches auto-deleted and cannot be restored one by one, so deliverable 3 (deliver by commit-ish, recording a COMMIT, shallow-safe and offline against main's own history) remains the only path that scales. Note also that this run re-verified deliver --dry-run as genuinely read-only (HEAD and the 462-line event count unchanged before and after), which sharpens finding A: seal is the only verb in the family that writes during --dry-run. INVARIANTS HELD throughout: no local branch was created for arena/841cc45d-synth (only refs/remotes/origin/...), HEAD stayed on the session branch arena/15e0fc51-synth, main stayed at 8b8dce26, the working tree stayed clean, and nothing was pushed to any branch.

PHASE 1 AUDIT RESULTS (executing, 2026-10-13), including a correction to consequence (a) recorded in the previous refinement, which measurement has falsified. CORRECTION - THE HARNESS CHANGE IS NOT A ONE-LINER. The previous note said pointing tests/helpers/cli-harness.js:24 at entry.js instead of synth.js would move 1536 calls onto the dispatcher and save ~75.6 ms each (~1.9 min per full run) and 'should not wait for phase 3'. That is unsafe as stated, because the two entry points do not agree. Measured with stdout and stderr separated and exit codes captured:   --version : entry.js rc=0 stdout '2.6.1' (plain text) | synth.js rc=0 stdout JSON envelope {status,version,name,schema:synth-cli-v1}. A stdout contract difference; 14 test files reference --version.   help      : entry.js rc=0 stdout 'synth v2.6.1' usage text | synth.js rc=1 stdout CLIError JSON 'Unknown command: help. Run synth --help for available commands.' The monolith FAILS on a verb the shipped CLI serves.   status    : rc=0 on both, stdout byte-equivalent in shape and BOTH PARSE CLEANLY as JSON. The only difference is stderr: synth.js emits 1 INFO line ('Resolving governance context for operator briefing'), entry.js emits none. Also correcting something asserted in conversation before it was measured: this line is NOT on stdout and does NOT break JSON.parse of stdout. It is stderr-only. FINDING 1 - THE SUITE TESTS AN ENTRY POINT THAT IS NOT SHIPPED. package.json bin maps synth -> dist/cli/entry.js, so the dispatcher is the CLI users run. The census shows 1536 of 1572 test spawns (98%) invoke dist/cli/synth.js instead. The shipped light path is therefore exercised by almost nothing, while the unshipped monolith path is what 106 suites assert on. Any behaviour difference between them is invisible to the governed chain. FINDING 2 - THE ONLY TEST OF THE SHIPPED ENTRY POINT IS AN ORPHAN. tests/loader-entrypoint.test.js:57 calls runEntry(['help']) - the single place in 242 files that runs the shipped entry point - and loader-entrypoint is on EXP-TEST-005's unreachable list (green, never run by test:all). So `synth help` is unguarded in the chain, which is consistent with the monolith returning rc=1 for it and nobody noticing. FINDING 3 - THE DECOMPOSITION WAS DONE BY DUPLICATION, NOT EXTRACTION, AND HAS ALREADY DRIFTED. src/cli/status-light.ts (labelled SYNTH-LOADER-002) is a line-by-line copy of cmdStatus in src/cli/synth.ts:3415 minus the Logger: both do sdk.paths.ensureDataDir(sdk.workspace.root()) -> buildOperatorBriefing(process.cwd()) -> buildStatusValidationSummary() -> attach .validation when status is ok -> printJson(briefing) -> process.exit(1) on error. The copy omits new Logger('status').info(...), which is exactly the stderr drift measured above. Two implementations of one verb will keep diverging; the fix is one implementation reached from both entry points, not a second lighter copy. FINDING 4 - THE LAZY-LOADING HAZARD IS NARROWER THAN THE GOAL FEARED. Scanned all 347 src/**/*.ts for module-scope side effects: exactly 5 module-scope process.cwd() captures, 0 module-scope process.env reads, 0 module-scope process.on() registrations. The 5 are infra/event-store.ts:13 EVENT_LOG_FILE and :14 EVENT_STREAM_DIR, infra/state-store.ts:12 STATE_FILE and :13 SNAPSHOTS_DIR, infra/checkpoint-store.ts:11 CHECKPOINT_FILE - three files, all of the form path.join(dataDir(process.cwd()), <name>). The 20 top-level `new Set/Map` values are immutable lookup tables (SPECIFICATION_SIGNALS, TEXT_EXTENSIONS, CONFIG_LANGUAGES, LIGHT_COMMANDS, DIVERGENCE_KINDS and similar), i.e. benign. So phase 1's audit reduces to making those 5 constants resolve per call instead of at import time, since lazy loading changes WHEN cwd is sampled. Note these are the same constants expedition 2c9c6c62 documented as the legacy read path. REVISED PLAN - PHASE 0 PRECEDES EVERYTHING: (a) one implementation per verb: cmdStatus and runStatus converge on a single extracted handler, and the stderr INFO line is either kept on both paths or dropped from both, by decision not by drift; (b) decide the canonical --version contract (plain string vs JSON envelope) and make both entry points agree, then update the 14 test files that reference it once, deliberately; (c) make `help` identical on both paths - rc=1 for `synth help` through the monolith is a user-facing bug for anything that bypasses the dispatcher; (d) only then repoint the harness at the shipped entry point so the suite tests what ships, and re-measure the saving. The ~1.9 min estimate still holds arithmetically but is now gated on (a)-(c), and it will improve once status-light stops pulling 134 modules / 916 KB. Loader-entrypoint must also be wired into the chain (EXP-TEST-005's remit) before the entry points are unified, so the unification is guarded by a test that actually runs.

D6. ARTIFACT-POLICY LEAK — test byproducts are written into a tracked, committable directory, and a
    ceremony commit then sweeps them into history. Three parts, all measured:
      (a) src/cli/certification-runner.ts:423 writes `certification-report-${Date.now()}.json` into
          options.outputDir, and tests/certification-framework.test.js:44 ASSERTS that a report file
          was written ("explain mode must write a report file"). That test is chained, so every full
          `npm run test:all` leaves three new untracked timestamped files under
          proof/certifications/. Observed twice in two consecutive sessions (1791937544354/5/6 and
          1791969422089/8/9), cleaned both times.
      (b) Commit 5907889 ("EXPEDITION_REFINED expedition 2c13ca22") committed three of them —
          526 lines each, 1578 lines of byproduct — alongside 3 ledger files. Mechanism:
          src/ledger/ceremony.ts:339-366 builds `existing` from the pathspecs its CALLER passes and
          commits with `git commit -m <msg> -- ...existing`. That caller's list included
          proof/certifications/, which is NOT in AUTO_COMMIT_INCLUDE_ROOTS
          (src/state/artifact-policy.ts:105 = [".synth/data", "proof/expeditions", "AGENTS.md"]).
          So there are two competing definitions of ceremony-commit scope and the broader one won.
      (c) scripts/check-artifact-policy.js PASSES over this (2195 tracked paths, "rules durable:13
          input:1 derived:1 cache:4 legacy:2"), because the reports classify as committable. No
          existing guard catches either half of this.
    Deliverable: make certification reports write to a temp dir (or classify proof/certifications as
    derived and ignore it), collapse ceremony-commit scope to ONE authority, and decide whether the
    1578 lines already in history under proof/certifications/ come back out. This is the same
    invariant class as "reads never write" and "derived state never blocks work" from the
    artifact-policy expedition; it is a leak of exactly what those invariants forbid.

MEASURED EVIDENCE 2026-10-14 — a verb created and checked out a branch it was told not to create,
and the ledger recorded a branch name that exists nowhere
============================================================
Observed while starting EXP-CLI-003 (e47a186cb472a20a) on this session branch. Reproduced, then
diagnosed from code and event offsets rather than inferred.

WHAT RAN
  synth expedition commit --proposal-id e47a186cb472a20a --branch arena/d5e4625c-synth --no-create
  -> rc=0, and its own output reported executionBranch {"branch":"arena/d5e4625c-synth","created":false}
  -> the reflog simultaneously recorded: "checkout: moving from arena/d5e4625c-synth to
     expedition/framework-maturation-v2-4ab7e9d/exp-cli-003-make-the-light-path-light-and-enforce-the-load-budgets-e47a186"
  The output contradicted the reflog. Both were telling the truth about different code paths.

TWO INDEPENDENT BRANCH PATHS INSIDE ONE VERB
  Path A — ADR-056 declaration, src/repository/branch-declaration.ts:92-112. Reads --branch and
    --no-create. Because currentBranch already equalled the declared branch it did nothing, and
    emitted event 485 EXPEDITION_BRANCH_BOUND {branch: arena/d5e4625c-synth, created: false,
    baseCommit: 189f7029ac21}. Correct.
  Path B — the ECOSYSTEM-001 canonical-branch auto-create, src/cli/synth.ts ~6552-6599, INSIDE
    cmdExpeditionCommit (which spans 6423..6923). Its own comment says "Auto-create the canonical
    expedition branch at start... When it runs, it switches to the canonical branch". It computes
    canonical = candidates[0] and calls adapter.branchExists / adapter.checkout(canonical) /
    adapter.createBranch(canonical). IT NEVER READS noCreate OR declaredBranch; its only guards are
    policy.mode === "enforce" && policy.strategy === "featured" and whether the current branch is
    already a canonical candidate. It emitted event 486 EXPEDITION_BRANCH_CREATED for the canonical
    name at the same baseCommit.
  Events 485 and 486 are adjacent offsets, which is what proves both paths fired in one invocation
  rather than the creation coming from a later command.

CONSEQUENCE: A SELF-INFLICTED DEADLOCK
  The ledger then bound execution to arena/d5e4625c-synth (Path A) while the checkout stood on the
  canonical branch (Path B). The next `expedition start` failed BRANCH_POLICY_DENIED: "expedition
  execution is bound to arena/d5e4625c-synth (ADR-056); current branch is expedition/framework-...
  Required branch: arena/d5e4625c-synth" — denying the transition because the verb had itself moved
  the checkout off the branch the ledger declared.
  Operator note, recorded honestly: the SECOND creation (event 487) was my error, not the framework's
  — I ran `expedition start --id e47a186c` bare, although ADR-056 §2.1 documents
  `expedition start --id ... --branch <name>` and cmdExpeditionStart does read flags.branch and
  flags["no-create"]. Run correctly, `start --id e47a186cb472a20a --branch arena/d5e4625c-synth
  --no-create` returned ok with executionBranch {created: false, declared: true}, did NOT switch
  branches, did NOT create anything, emitted event 488 EXPEDITION_BRANCH_BOUND, and moved the
  expedition to executing (autoCommit 23ad2d0c). So the deadlock is escapable — but only by an
  operator who knows to repeat the declaration on a second verb, after the first verb already
  ignored it once.

A BRANCH NAME RECORDED THAT EXISTS NOWHERE
  The canonical name is derived by slugifying mission + subject + id8
  (canonicalBranchCandidates, src/repository/branch-taxonomy.ts:133) and then materialized to make
  the derivation true. It was recorded twice (events 486 and 487, baseCommits 189f7029ac21 and
  1423d53d6611). It was never pushed: `git ls-remote --heads origin | grep -c exp-cli-003` = 0. It no
  longer exists locally (deleted twice during recovery). And the expedition record itself never
  mentions it — 0 occurrences of the string in .synth/data/expeditions/e47a186cb472a20a.json — so the
  contradiction lives only in the event stream, where nothing reconciles BOUND against CREATED.
  This is the operator's diagnosis confirmed: the branch layer GUESSES names from strings and creates
  reality to match, instead of asking git what exists. The hash layer is the only factual part, which
  is exactly why containment-by-tipCommit worked for 4 of 4 sealed expeditions while every
  name-based path in this session either failed (DELIVERY_PUSH_FAILED) or needed a human to go read
  GitHub (--merge-commit).

WHAT THIS EXPEDITION MUST THEREFORE DO, BEYOND ITS ORIGINAL DELIVERABLES
  * One authority for branch decisions. A verb must not contain two paths that can disagree; if a
    declared branch exists, the canonical auto-create path must not run, and `--no-create` must bind
    every path in the verb, not just the one that implements it.
  * A verb's output must describe what it DID, not what one of its paths intended. Returning
    created:false while a checkout happened is worse than either behaviour alone, because it sends
    the operator looking for the wrong cause.
  * Never record a branch name that was not verified to exist, and never leave BOUND and CREATED
    events unreconciled. If a name is derived, either verify it against git or do not write it.
  * Declaration must not have to be repeated per verb. `--branch`/`--no-create` given at commit time
    is already in the ledger (EXPEDITION_BRANCH_BOUND); `start` should read that binding instead of
